'''Jerrold Meinwald''' (January 16, 1927 – April 23, 2018) was an American [[chemist]] known for his work on [[chemical ecology]], a field he co-founded with his colleague and friend [[Thomas Eisner]]. He was a Goldwin Smith [[Emeritus Professor|Professor Emeritus of Chemistry]] at [[Cornell University]]. He was author or co-author of well over 400 scientific articles. His interest in chemistry was sparked by fireworks done with his friend [[Michael P. Cava]] when they were still in junior high school. Meinwald was also a music aficionado and studied flute with [[Marcel Moyse]] – the world's greatest flutist of his time.{{according to who|date=May 2019}}

==Career==
Jerrold Meinwald was born in 1927 in New York City.<ref>"[https://web.archive.org/web/20131104140704/http://chemistry.ua.edu/department/seminars-and-lectures/2009-cava-lecturer-meinwald/ 2009 Cava Lecturer (Meinwald)]", ''[[University of Alabama]]'' (October, 2009).</ref> He studied chemistry at the University of Chicago where he earned his Bachelor of Science degree in 1948. He then went on to [[Harvard University]] where he obtained his Ph.D. with [[R.B. Woodward]] in 1952. A DuPont Fellowship brought him to Cornell, where he has spent most of his subsequent career.
[[File:Chlaenius Plate 10 Eisner et al 1963.png|thumb|left|Series from a study by Meinwald and Eisner investigating defensive spray in ''[[Chlaenius]]'' beetles with paper that turns dark in response to chemicals.]]
Since the early 1960s, he has worked, often in collaboration with [[Thomas Eisner]], on chemical signalling in animals, particularly insects and arthropods; he is regarded as one of the founders of the field of chemical ecology. A particular field of interest was the ways in which insects either use chemicals synthesised by the plants that they feed on, or use those plant chemicals as substrates from which to synthesize their own. A species on which he and Eisner published several times over decades is the moth ''[[Utetheisa ornatrix]]'', which [[Pyrrolizidine alkaloid sequestration|collects pyrrolizidine alkaloids]] from its food source<ref name=acquired>{{cite journal | vauthors = Dussourd DE, Ubik K, Harvis C, Resch J, Meinwald J, Eisner T | title = Biparental defensive endowment of eggs with acquired plant alkaloid in the moth Utetheisa ornatrix | journal = Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. | volume = 85 | issue = 16 | pages = 5992–6 | year = 1988 | pmid = 3413071 | pmc = 281891 | doi = 10.1073/pnas.85.16.5992| bibcode = 1988PNAS...85.5992D | doi-access = free }}</ref> and uses them as a deterrent to predators; the male also uses them as a pheromone<ref name=pheromone>{{cite journal | vauthors = Conner WE, Eisner T, Vander Meer RK, Guerrero A, Meinwald J | title = Precopulatory sexual interaction in an arctiid moth (Utetheisa ornatrix): Role of a pheromone derived from dietary alkaloids | journal = Behavioral Ecology and Sociobiology | volume = 9 | issue = 3 | pages = 227–235 | doi = 10.1007/BF00302942| year = 1981 | s2cid = 22839356 }}</ref> and passes them on in its semen to the female who uses them to make her eggs unpalatable.<ref name=acquired /><ref name=sexual-selection>{{cite journal | vauthors = Eisner T, Meinwald J | title = The chemistry of sexual selection | journal = Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. | volume = 92 | issue = 1 | pages = 50–5 | year = 1995 | pmid = 7816847 | pmc = 42815 | doi = 10.1073/pnas.92.1.50| bibcode = 1995PNAS...92...50E | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref name=nuptial-gift>{{cite journal | vauthors = Dussourd DE, Harvis CA, Meinwald J, Eisner T | title = Pheromonal advertisement of a nuptial gift by a male moth (Utetheisa ornatrix) | journal = Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. | volume = 88 | issue = 20 | pages = 9224–7 | year = 1991 | pmid = 1924385 | pmc = 52686 | doi = 10.1073/pnas.88.20.9224| bibcode = 1991PNAS...88.9224D | doi-access = free }}</ref>

In analysing the constituents of plant signalling, he developed a number of retrosynthetic techniques, including the '''Meinwald Rearrangement''' where an [[epoxide]] is converted to a [[carbonyl]] in the presence of a [[Lewis acid]]; he has also performed substantial research over forty years in NMR spectroscopy.<ref name=bicyclohexane>{{cite journal | vauthors = Meinwald J, Lewis A | title = Long-range spin-spin couplings in the nuclear magnetic resonance spectra of bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes | journal = Journal of the American Chemical Society | volume = 83 | issue = 12 | pages = 2769–2770 | doi = 10.1021/ja01473a039| year = 1961 }}</ref> and in reactions for producing chiral derivatives in order to determine [[absolute configuration]]s of chiral molecules.<ref name=chiral-silylation>{{cite journal | vauthors = Weibel DB, Walker TR, Schroeder FC, Meinwald J | title = Chiral Silylation Reagents for the Determination of Absolute Configuration by NMR Spectroscopy | journal = Org. Lett. | volume = 2 | issue = 15 | pages = 2381–3 | year = 2000 | pmid = 10930289 | doi = 10.1021/ol006162h}}</ref><ref name=chiral-silylation-web>{{cite web | url = http://www.nightvzn.net/portfolio/web/meinwald_group/research_projects_chiral_silylation.html | title = Chiral Silylation Reagents for the Determination of Absolute Configuration Using NMR Spectroscopy | work = The Meinwald Group | publisher = Cornell University }}</ref>

In 1981, Meinwald became a founding member of the [[World Cultural Council]].<ref>{{cite web | title = About Us | publisher = [[World Cultural Council]] | url = http://www.consejoculturalmundial.org/about-us/ | access-date = November 8, 2016 | archive-date = June 29, 2019 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190629135114/https://www.consejoculturalmundial.org/about-us/ | url-status = dead }}</ref> He died in Ithaca on April 23, 2018, at the age of 91.<ref>{{cite news | last=Fleischman | first=Tom | name-list-style = vanc | date=2018-04-25 | title=Jerrold Meinwald, 2014 National Medal of Science winner, dies at 91 |url=https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2018/04/jerrold-meinwald-2014-national-medal-science-winner-dies-91 |work=Cornell Chronicle|access-date=2018-04-27 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/05/14/obituaries/jerrold-meinwald-91-dies-studied-creatures-chemical-signals.html|title=Jerrold Meinwald, 91, Dies; Studied Creatures' Chemical Signals|first=Kenneth|last=Chang|date=May 14, 2018|newspaper=The New York Times}}</ref>

{{Clear}}

==Awards==
He won the [[National Medal of Science]] in 2012.<ref name="urlJerrold Meinwald wins National Medal of Science | Cornell Chronicle">{{cite web | url = https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2014/10/jerrold-meinwald-wins-national-medal-science | title = Jerrold Meinwald wins National Medal of Science | work = Cornell Chronicle | date = October 6, 2014}}</ref><ref name="President Obama Honors Nation’s Top Scientists and Innovators | The White House">{{cite web | url= https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/2014/10/03/president-obama-honors-nation-s-top-scientists-and-innovators | work= [[whitehouse.gov]] | title = President Obama Honors Nation's Top Scientists and Innovators | via= [[NARA|National Archives]] | date = October 3, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = Gerrold Meinwald, 2012, National Medal of Science Chemistry | url = http://nationalmedals.org/laureates/jerrold-meinwald | publisher =National Science & Technology Medal Foundation }}</ref> He was a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] since 1969, Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] since 1970, and member of the [[American Philosophical Society]] since 1987. Other notable honours:
* Distinguished Leadership Award, [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (2016)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.amacad.org/content/about/about.aspx?d=22210&t=4&s=0|title=Recipients of the Distinguished Leadership Award - American Academy of Arts & Sciences|date=September 21, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170921125824/http://www.amacad.org/content/about/about.aspx?d=22210&t=4&s=0|archive-date=September 21, 2017}}</ref>
* Grand Prix de la Fondation de la Maison de la Chimie, Paris, France (2006)
* [[Nakanishi Prize]], American Chemical Society (2014)
* Roger Adams Award in Organic Chemistry, [[American Chemical Society]] (2005)
* Chemical Pioneer Award, [[American Institute of Chemists]] (1997)
* Silver Medal of the International Society of Chemical Ecology (1991)
* [[Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement]] (1990)
* A. C. Cope Scholar Award, American Chemical Society (1989)
* Fellow, [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (1970)

== Publications ==
* Eisner, T, & Meinwald, J, Eds. (1995) ''Chemical Ecology: The Chemistry of Biotic Interaction''. National Academy Press.
